messages:
anya: Heads-up — spike notes from the policy sharding experiment. Thinking out loud: how do we make per-tenant routing policies sharded by region without blowing up consistency or making rollouts impossible?
kevin: quick summary of constraints pls — latency/cost/regulatory?
sam: +1 to Kevin. Also curious if you mean runtime sharding (split policy eval state) or compile-time split (generate per-region policy blobs).
anya: all of the above. Primary goals: keep eval fast (sub-ms for common cases), let operators patch rules safely, and preserve deterministic fallback ordering so SLAs don't break. Secondary: minimize cross-region state sync.
maria: FWIW the current policy runtime is a single in-memory graph per process. Sharding would need either: 1) precompiled region-specific graphs deployed to nodes, or 2) a hot-path RPC to a centralized decision service. Tradeoffs: (1) faster and offline-safe but harder to roll out; (2) easier rollout but adds network dependency.
kevin: +1. My gut: prefer precompiled per-region blobs for host-level decisions and keep a small centralized fallback for rare global overrides. That way normal routes are local.
anya: that matches my thinking. Two practical questions: how to handle policy preflight (simulating a rollout across traffic) and how to version blobs so old nodes can still evaluate correctly during a mixed-version rollout.
sam: For preflight, we should reuse the existing sim harness (eval-sim) but extend it to run against a region-aware topology. Example run: `./eval-sim --policy new_policy.pb --topology us-east,eu-west --sample 1m` and compare route diffs and expected latency delta.
anya: sample output I had from a tiny sim run (us-east only):
```
- 98.6% requests keep same route
- 1.1% switch to cheaper-but-slower fallback (median +12ms)
- 0.3% would hit capacity guard and be preempted
```
kevin: Sounds reasonable. We need thresholds for automated rollback: e.g., if >0.5% requests move to preempted state or median latency increases by >10ms then fail canary.
maria: versioning: embed a `policy_schema_version` and `compat_flags` in the blob header. Evaluators read header, and if incompatible they fall back to the centralized safe-eval RPC which is guaranteed to understand all historic flags. That gives us an escape hatch.
sam: How about cache invalidation? When we push a new blob we must evict any prefix caches that depend on policy semantics (route affinity, prefetch hints). Hard to do without per-node coordination.
kevin: propose a soft-evict approach: attach a monotonic `policy_epoch` in the blob. Evaluators treat cached entries with epoch < current - 1 as stale. That avoids immediate global invalidation and still degrades gracefully.
anya: I like epoching. Implementation notes: we should add a tiny header to the runtime cache entries: `cached_epoch`. Eviction policy: if `cached_epoch < blob.epoch` then prefer recompute but don't block if compute would exceed latency SLO — instead mark as stale and continue using old entry while scheduling async recompute.
maria: one more thing — telemetry. We need structured diffs for preflight so SRE can inspect. Fields: `route_before`, `route_after`, `predicted_latency_delta_ms`, `reasons_changed` (list). Dump as newline-delimited JSON to telemetry.
sam: example policy DSL snippet that causes most trouble is greedy affinity fallback. If we allow high-weight affinity rules they mask lower-cost routes. Maybe add a normalized weight cap per-tenant.
anya: suggested snippet (pseudo-DSL):
```
policy {
  id: "tenant-xyz"
  rules: [
    { match: {model: "gpt-lite"}, weight: 1.0 },
    { match: {model: "gpt-proxy"}, weight: 0.05, region_preference: ["eu-west"] }
  ]
  guards: { max_affinity_weight: 0.4 }
  epoch: 42
}
```
kevin: +1 on `max_affinity_weight`. Default should be 0.5 but allow enterprise override with a `guarded_override` that requires a config sig + audit log.
maria: ops checklist for rollout: 1) run sim on 10% sample traffic, 2) push blobs to canary region nodes, 3) monitor diffs and preemptions, 4) if thresholds pass promote to 50% then global. Also add a fast rollback RPC that can force `policy_epoch` bump to revert.
sam: owners? I can take preflight sim extension. Kevin can own runtime blob format + epoching. Maria can sketch rollout playbook + thresholds. Anya will own the policy DSL changes and guard flags.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary push scheduled for 3210011000.
anya: thanks — I'll open an RFC PR that includes the DSL changes, epoch header, and the sim extension API. Also will add the telemetry schema and a small migration plan for mixed-version clusters.
kevin: thumbs-up. One follow-up: document the fallback latency budget for safe-eval RPC (p95 < 10ms) so it's actually usable. If the RPC can't meet that we need a different escape plan.
maria: noted — I'll run a perf test and add numbers to the RFC.
anya: ok wrapping up — action items in thread. Short and practical. Thanks all :rocket:
